newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Jail terms sought for S.Korean campus protesters.
newsitem.headline: Jail terms sought for S.Korean campus protesters.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors sought prison terms for about 50 out of 76 university students who went on trial on Friday in connection to violent campus demonstrations in August, court officials said.
State prosecutors in Seoul District Court demanded that about 50 defendants serve two to five years in jail for their role in the protests at Seoul's Yonsei University, the officials said.

The charges ranged from acts of violence, such as wielding steel pipes against police and throwing fire bombs, to interference in police duties and violating the National Security Law, officials said.

The trials for the worst campus protests to hit South Korea since President Kim Young-sam took power in February 1993 began on Tuesday, when prosecutors asked the court to deliver two-six year prison terms to about 50 of 62 students in court that day.

About 3,225 students were arrested in August after riot police stormed the campus to end seven days of occupation by the students, who demanded reunification with North Korea and the withdrawal of U.S. troops stationed in South Korea.
A total of 444 students have been charged in connection with the demonstrations.

Thirty-eight students face charges under the National Security law which bars all unapproved contacts with North Korea, while 10 have been charged in connection with the murder of a policeman who died of head wounds during the protests.

Of the 444 students, 241 are being tried at Seoul District Court and 203 are being handled at its four branches. The trial will open twice a week until the end of the month and sentences were expected to be announced from October 29.
The remaining students face charges over their involvement in the demonstrations.
